title.narrative: CAFOD - Tu Faulu Pamoja - Ungdomar och kvinnor, lyckas tillsammans – Fas 2
CAFOD - Tu Faulu Pamoja - Youth and women, Succeeding together – Phase 2

description.narrative:
Den katolska biståndsorganisationen för utveckling utomlands (CAFOD) har lämnat in ett projektförslag som syftar till att stärka kvinnors och ungdomars deltagande i beslutsfattande positioner för att främja demokrati och fredsbyggande i Demokratiska republiken Kongo (DRK).
CAFOD kommer att arbeta direkt med tre lokala civilsamhällesorganisationer: Rien Sans Les Femmes (RSLF)-rörelsen, Union des Jeunes Congolais pour le Changement (UJCC) och Commission Episcopale Justice et Paix (CEJP).
Projektet syftar till att säkerställa att kvinnors och ungdomars röster förstås väl och att deras specifika behov beaktas för utveckling och fred i DRK. Det kommer att tillhandahålla en evidensbaserad, transformativ modell för institutionellt stöd och kapacitetsstärkande, som främjar ett rättighetsbaserat och samhällsledt tillvägagångssätt som främjar kvinnors och ungdomars deltagande i civila och offentliga beslutsprocesser på alla nivåer. Detta tillvägagångssätt är konfliktsensitivt och främjar fredsbyggande genom gemensamt samarbete och engagemang. Projektet kommer vidare att främja samarbete mellan flera intressenter, inklusive civilsamhällesorganisationer och rörelser, samhällsmedlemmar och regeringsrepresentanter på alla nivåer.
Specifika mål inkluderar:
Stärka riktade kvinnors rörelser och ungdomsorganisationer för effektivt deltagande och representation i beslutsfattande och fredsbyggande processer på alla nivåer till 2023. Förbättra förståelsen av utvecklande lagar bland riktade kvinnors rörelser och ungdomsorganisationer, identifiera brister, bedriva relevant påverkansarbete och delta i beslutsfattande utrymmen på alla nivåer. Förbättra ekonomisk egenmakt för kvinnor och ungdomar i riktade samhällen genom förbättrade affärsutvecklingsfärdigheter och deltagande i samhällsdrivna och miljövänliga mikroföretag. Projektet kommer att rikta sig till sex samordningspunkter för Rien Sans Les Femmes (RSLF)-rörelsen i sex provinser, som omfattar 180 organisationer och 500 000 kvinnliga medlemmar. Det kommer också att rikta sig till sex provinsiella ungdomsplattformar i sex provinser, som omfattar 7 200 ungdomar (1 200 per provins). Projektet kommer att verka i sex provinser: Kinshasa, Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Tanganyika, Tshopo och Ituri.
Indirekta förmånstagare kommer att inkludera minst 5 miljoner människor som nås genom kvinnofokuserade aktiviteter, bestående av 60% kvinnor, 15% män och 25% unga flickor och pojkar. Detta inkluderar uppskattningsvis 1 miljon människor som nås via fokuserade sociala medieaktiviteter. Ytterligare 100 000 ungdomar kommer att nås genom ungdomsengagemangsaktiviteter och länkar med universitet, inklusive uppskattningsvis 28 000 som nås via fokuserade sociala medieaktiviteter. De totala indirekta förmånstagarna uppskattas till 5 100 000 personer.
Sida bedömer nätverket och rollen för CAFOD som en trosbaserad organisation (FBO) med många års erfarenhet av utvecklings-, humanitära och fredsinsatser globalt. Som en stark förespråkare för genus rättvisa är CAFOD en relevant partner engagerad i transformativt arbete för jämställdhet. Progressiva trosbaserade rörelser som främjar en positiv diskurs för jämställdhet behöver stöd, särskilt mitt i en växande motreaktion mot jämställdhet och krympande utrymme för civilsamhället, inklusive från trosbaserade grupper.
Som ett trosbaserat nätverk är CAFOD i en nyckelposition för att ta itu med genusorättvisor genom att överbrygga diskursen om religion med den om sekulära och mänskliga rättigheter, och genom att mobilisera trosledare. Genom att bidra till förändrade samhällsnormer, policyer och praxis genom denna intervention kommer CAFOD och dess partners att hjälpa till att uppnå SDG5 och den övergripande visionen om en värld där jämställdhet och rättvisa är förverkligade, mänskliga rättigheter åtnjuts lika och människor har makten att fritt forma samhällen, trosgemenskaper och sina egna liv.

The Catholic Agency for Overseas Development (CAFOD) has submitted a project proposal aimed at strengthening the participation of women and young people in decision-making positions to promote democracy and peacebuilding in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
CAFOD will work directly with three local civil society organizations: the Rien Sans Les Femmes (RSLF) movement, the Union des Jeunes Congolais pour le Changement (UJCC), and the Commission Episcopale Justice et Paix (CEJP).
The project aims to ensure that the voices of women and young people are well understood and that their specific needs are considered for development and peace in the DRC. It will provide an evidence-based, transformational model of institutional support and capacity strengthening, fostering a rights-based and community-led approach that promotes women’s and youth participation in civic and public decision-making processes at all levels. This approach is conflict-sensitive and promotes peacebuilding through joint collaboration and engagement. The project will further promote collaboration among multiple stakeholders, including civil society organizations and movements, community members, and government representatives at all levels.
Specific objectives include:
Empowering targeted women’s movements and youth organizations for effective participation and representation in decision-making and peacebuilding processes at all levels by 2023. Enhancing the understanding of evolving laws among targeted women’s movements and youth organizations, identifying gaps, undertaking relevant advocacy, and participating in decision-making spaces at all levels. Enhancing economic empowerment for women and youth in targeted communities through improved business development skills and participation in community-driven and environmentally friendly micro-enterprises. The project will target six coordination points of the Rien Sans Les Femmes (RSLF) movement in six provinces, involving 180 organizations and 500,000 women members. It will also target six provincial youth platforms in six provinces, involving 7,200 youth (1,200 per province). The project will operate in six provinces: Kinshasa, Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Tanganyika, Tshopo, and Ituri.
Indirect beneficiaries will include at least 5 million people reached through women-focused activities, constituting 60% women, 15% men, and 25% young girls and boys. This includes an estimated 1 million people reached via focused social media activities. An additional 100,000 youth will be reached through youth engagement activities and links with universities, including an estimated 28,000 reached via focused social media activities. The total indirect beneficiaries are estimated at 5,100,000 people.
Sida assesses the network and role of CAFOD as a Faith-Based Organization (FBO) with many years of experience in development, humanitarian, and peace interventions globally. As a strong advocate for gender justice, CAFOD is a relevant partner engaged in transformational work for gender equality. Progressive faith-based movements promoting a positive discourse for gender equality need support, especially amid a growing backlash on gender equality and shrinking space for civil society, including from faith-based groups.
As a faith-based network, CAFOD is in a key position to address gender injustices by bridging the discourse of religion with that of secular and human rights, and by mobilizing faith leaders. By contributing to changed societal norms, policies, and practices through this intervention, CAFOD and its partners will help achieve SDG5 and the overall vision of a world where gender equality and justice are realized, human rights are equally enjoyed, and people have the power to freely shape societies, faith communities, and their own lives.

The primary objective of this intervention is to build upon the achievements of the first phase of the Tu Faulu Pamoja project, increasing its impact and sustainability by focusing on women and youth in civic and political participation, as well as peacebuilding processes. Special attention will be given to girls, as they are often overlooked in such initiatives.
By employing a human rights-based and gender-responsive approach, the project prioritizes the promotion and protection of women and girls rights while strengthening local and national institutions to eliminate violence against them. Empowering women and youth as leaders in the political and peacebuilding arenas is expected to shift the trajectory of poverty and exclusion in the DRC. Women's political participation, for instance, has been shown to generate tangible benefits for democratic governance.
Increased women's participation in decision-making roles tends to result in better social investments, which will benefit the broader population. Research also shows that greater gender balance in political spheres leads to more equitable representation in the workforce, which could potentially double the DRC's GDP by 2025 if women are empowered to their full potential.
The project also seeks to prevent violence against women and girls by influencing attitudes and behaviors, through collaboration with men and boys, youth, and faith-based organizations. This will be achieved by creating men and boy gender champions and school clubs.
Finally, the project aligns with the PDDRCS framework through its focus on stabilization and conflict prevention, promoting peaceful coexistence, social cohesion, and the economic recovery of communities.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
CAFOD's result from 2024 included several Youth Engagement and Empowerment Activities, such as:
1) Safe Spaces for Youth Dialogue: At the Maison de la Femme in Goma (supported under TFP Phase 1), youth engaged in dialogues on local insecurity issues such as killings, kidnappings, and abuses. These sessions led to: oIncreased knowledge of support mechanisms. oSharing of resources (contacts/networks). oEnhanced openness, communication, and accountability among youth. oProvision of therapeutic support for trauma and distress.
2) Promotion of Female Participation: Youth awareness was improved through dissemination of GBV reports. These emphasized: oThe importance of engaging women and girls in decision-making. oThe impact of gender based violence on women. oThe value of social cohesion, especially in conflict-affected provinces such as Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu.
3) Establishment of Peace Clubs: Peace clubs were created in schools to promote positive masculinity and peaceful conflict resolution. 4) Environmental Protection Initiatives: Youth received materials and support to engage in environmental safeguarding activities.
CAFOD also provided support through CEJP (Commission Episcopale Justice et Paix). As a key TFP project partner, CEJP played a central role in advancing peace and advocacy efforts by:
1) Developing advocacy strategies and implementation plans in coordination with CENCO. 2) Designing and disseminating advocacy messages focused on peace and social justice. 3) Organizing stakeholder engagement meetings, both with government and civil society. 4) COnducting media and outreach programmes targeting diverse audiences. 5) Leveraging CEJP/CENCOs national and diocesan networks to amplify project reach and ensure sustainability and ownership of results.
CAFOD also supported CEJP with: Capacity building (organizational development, resource mobilization, programme management); Advocacy training (development of advocacy tools, strategies, and stakeholder linkages); Funding support (both through SIDA and internal CAFOD resources).
CAFOD also supported a joint initiative between the National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) and the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC), aiming to promote peace and democratic processes. This initiative is known as the Social Pact for Peace and Good Living Together in the DRC and the Great Lakes Region, which seeks to: oAddress the root causes of conflict in Eastern DRC. oPromote lasting peace, national/regional cohesion, and peaceful coexistence.
In relation, a comprehensive report on activities (domestic and international) was submitted to President Tshisekedi. A national forum has also been proposed to facilitate inclusive dialogue among Congolese citizens
Overall, CAFOD and its partners have made significant strides in: •Empowering youth and promoting gender inclusion. •Strengthening civil society advocacy capacity through CEJP. •Supporting national and faith-based peacebuilding initiatives (CENCO/ECC).
These multi-level efforts contribute toward the broader TFP project goals of fostering peace, justice, inclusion, and sustainable change in the DRC.
A more comprehensive project report will be submitted in March 2026.
